Xanthoma lesions, as identified by histological examination, contained foam-cell infiltration or necrobiosis, cholesterol clefts and Touton giant cells in both NX and NXG (Fig.1). All patients had serum MIg, as was detected by electrophoresis and confirmed by immunofixation (IF). The MIg isotype (IgG, 6 κ and 10 λ), hypocomplementaemia and underlying haematological conditions (MGUS, n = 9; multiple myeloma, n = 6; and lymphoma, n = 1) are detailed in Table1. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Low-power histology view (20×) of NXG lesion showing collagenous fibrous tissue and overall architecture. B: Medium-power histology view (80×) showing epidermis and dermal infiltrate consistent with NXG. C: High-power histology view (140×) demonstrating abundant foamy histiocytes (blue arrow) and multinucleated giant cells (green arrow), characteristic of NXG. D: High-power histology view (160×) demonstrating abundant foamy histiocytes (blue arrow) and multinucleated giant cells (green arrow), characteristic of NXG.

An incisional punch biopsy (right lower eyelid) confirmed the diagnosis of NXG. Histopathology indeed shows a diffuse xanthomatized histiocytic infiltrate focally admixed with lymphocytes throughout the dermis into the subcutis. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: H&E stained histology demonstrating classic NXG features including geographic collagen necrobiosis, Touton giant cells, cholesterol clefts, and foamy histiocytic infiltrate within the dermis. B: CD68 immunohistochemistry confirming the histiocytic nature of the dermal infiltrate in the NXG lesion.

Cholesterol clefts are present within the inflammatory infiltrate. B, CD68 stains for histiocytes are positive.
